title: D²ACCI: A Dual-Loop Diagnostic Protocol for Evidence-Preserving Agent Memory

visual_explainer.blocker: Two isolated paper-specific GPT Image attempts in this run (CABLE and ArborMem) both ignored their grounded single-paper briefs and rendered a generic Agent Memory Radar dashboard with fabricated paper metadata. Visual QA rejected both; further required-paper retries were stopped to avoid publishing ungrounded visuals until the paper-identity failure is resolved.

analysis.tldr: D²ACCI turns memory evaluation into a promotion protocol: typed stage traces feed an outer diagnostic loop that requires paired baseline/candidate evidence, protected slices, trace coverage, and deterministic accept/feature-flag/reject gates instead of promoting a memory change from an endpoint score alone.
analysis.problem: Memory pipelines can improve an aggregate benchmark while hiding which stage changed, where regressions occur, or whether logs are sufficient to diagnose failures. Result-only evaluation therefore encourages causal over-attribution and silent regression.
analysis.core_idea: Instrument an inner memory runtime with typed traces across ingestion, storage, retrieval, filtering, context construction, and generation. An outer loop proposes a hypothesis and protected slices, runs paired baseline/candidate artifacts, applies paired statistical tests and Diagnostic Coverage Rate (DCR), and uses deterministic gates to accept, accept-with-monitoring, feature-flag, reject, or archive the change.

memory_design.write: Not a new memory representation; the protocol records typed stage traces and paired candidate/baseline artifacts around memory changes.
memory_design.organize: Organize evidence by pipeline stage, protected slice, paired outcome, trace coverage, and decision-gate result so regressions remain attributable.
memory_design.read: Diagnostics consume stage traces plus paired statistics to determine whether a proposed memory change should be promoted, monitored, feature-flagged, or rejected.
memory_design.update_forget: The outer loop governs memory-system changes rather than end-user memory deletion; null/rejected interventions are retained as diagnostic priors instead of silently discarded.

compared_to: Result-only evaluation without actionable stage traces
Paired baseline/candidate feature interventions including supplement extraction, session retrieval, Forget Guard, and BM25/RRF changes
Human relabeling under enriched traces versus result-only artifacts
analysis.evidence: Three interventions clear the protocol with significant paired gains: supplement extraction +2.71pp (p=.0009), session retrieval +3.67pp (p=.0026), and Forget Guard +1.92pp (p=.0030). BM25/RRF changes are null on LoCoMo (-0.41, p=.4426) and LongMemEval (+1.00, p=.4583) and are feature-flagged rather than promoted. In a 60-case audit, enriched traces improve inter-rater agreement to κ=.571 fine/.619 coarse versus .258/.272 for result-only artifacts. A PersonaMem diagnosis assigns 87% of observed failures to post-retrieval stages, illustrating why retrieval-only attribution is incomplete.
analysis.why_it_matters: D²ACCI operationalizes a principle the radar has been using editorially: a memory change should earn promotion only when paired evidence identifies benefit without protected-slice harm and the trace is rich enough to localize the cause. It also treats null results as useful deployment evidence.
limitations: Diagnostic Coverage Rate depends on the instrumentation schema, so the contrast with result-only logging is partly built into the metric definition.
The protocol is demonstrated on one instrumented stack and does not yet establish cross-framework portability.
Statistical gates improve evaluation discipline but do not replace deployment-time user utility, privacy, or online safety monitoring.
Headline system scores mix many components; the strongest contribution is the diagnostic protocol, not a new memory architecture.
